summary.intent: Fix a broken statusline and a stop-hook error (gsd-context-monitor.js MODULE_NOT_FOUND), update GSD to restore the missing hook, clean up stale worktrees, then plan and fully implement Phase 61 (AAD-Bound Seal Primitive and Cross-Language KAT) through to a shipped PR.
summary.outcome: Statusline fixed (renamed .js → .cjs to resolve ESM/CJS conflict), GSD reinstalled to 1.6.0 (restoring all missing hooks and the file manifest), three worktrees removed cleanly, Phase 61 fully implemented across 5 plans/4 waves with 197 TS + 97 Rust tests green, PR #576 opened with all 29 CI checks passing and 6/6 review threads resolved.

repo: package.json has "type": "module" — Node treats all .js files in the project as ESM. Hooks using require() must use the .cjs extension or Node crashes with 'require is not defined in ES module scope'.
.claude/hooks/gsd-* files are gitignored (line 55) and installed locally by GSD — they cannot be restored via git, only by re-running the GSD installer.

The GSD main-tree install was a broken fragment (no gsd-tools.cjs, no update workflow, no manifest). Complete installs existed only in throwaway worktrees (on GSD 1.4.3). Clean reinstall: `npx @opengsd/gsd-core@<ver> -- gsd-core --claude --local`.

CONTEXT.md cited the TS test path as `packages/crypto/__tests__/build-node-aad.test.ts` but vitest's `include: ['src/**/*.ts']` only discovers files under `src/`. Correct path: `packages/crypto/src/__tests__/build-node-aad.test.ts`.

scripts/check-vector-parity.sh has a hardcoded EXPECTED_VECTORS array — every new vector file (e.g. node-aad.json) must be registered there or the parity CI step fails even when both Rust and TS tests pass.
Fixed-IV KAT vectors must test the lower-level `encryptAesGcmAad`/`decrypt_aes_gcm_aad`, NOT `sealAesGcmAad` — the seal wrapper mints a fresh random IV and cannot produce a deterministic output.
The uuid crate (v1.23.4) is the only new workspace dependency introduced by phase 61; requires addition to both root Cargo.toml workspace and crates/crypto/Cargo.toml.
Root tsconfig.scripts.json fails `@types/node` resolution because @types/node v20 is in the pnpm store but not hoisted to root node_modules/@types/. Pre-existing, not triggered by phase 61.
gh pr edit fails on this repo (Projects-classic GraphQL). Patch PR body via: `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh api -X PATCH repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/<N> -F body=@file`.
github-actions[bot] pushes a `chore(release)` commit to the branch after PR creation and after passing Release Preview — must `git fetch` + rebase before any subsequent push or it is rejected.

Branch protection on main: required_signatures=false, 0 required reviews. The only ruleset is `tags` (not branch PRs). Unsigned commits do NOT block this merge — memory of 'enforced signatures' was stale.
CodeRabbit 'Review skipped' on a PR check is transient — the review may complete later after CI runs on the new head.

The existing encryptAesGcm (packages/crypto/src/aes/encrypt.ts) uses `new Uint8Array(key)` without zeroization — established project convention. Adding zeroization only to new AAD variants creates inconsistency.
mergeStateStatus BLOCKED immediately after a push means CI is still running on the new head, not a real merge blocker — confirm by checking rollup: PENDING.

code.finding: TS KAT for AAD builder and seal vectors. Must assert exact array lengths (toHaveLength(4) for aad_vectors, toBe(1) for seal_vectors) and role-set ([1,2,3,4]) to prevent vacuous-pass on empty/truncated arrays. Also pins [IV][ct+tag] envelope order via unsealAesGcmAad round-trip.

Rust cross-language KAT. Must assert exact counts (assert_eq!(aad_vectors.len(), 4); assert_eq!(seal_vectors.len(), 1)) and the full role-set, not just !is_empty(). Also pins envelope order via unseal_aes_gcm_aad round-trip.

uuidToBytes validates input with /^[0-9a-fA-F]{32}$/ regex and throws CryptoError INVALID_AAD_INPUT for invalid input. Accepts slightly different non-canonical UUID forms than the Rust side (LOW-1 deferred).

Hardcoded EXPECTED_VECTORS array. Adding tests/vectors/crypto/node-aad.json to this array is a required CI integration task — omitting it causes parity CI failure even when both TS and Rust tests pass.
.claude/hooks/gsd-* is gitignored. GSD-managed hooks must be reinstalled via the GSD installer after any fresh clone, not restored via git.

Renamed from statusline.js to force CommonJS treatment. Required because repo-root package.json has type:module, making .js files ESM where require() is unavailable. Project settings.json overrides global statusline with this path.

workflow: CodeRabbit CLI: always use `--base origin/main`, not `--base main`. A stale local main can inflate the diff from the actual 44 changed files to 661, triggering the file-limit guard and producing useless output.
GSD commit helper false-negatives are common — it can report 'commit_failed' while the commit actually lands. Always verify with `git log --oneline -1`, never blindly retry.

1Password SSH signing blocks commits in AFK background subagents (requires biometric approval). For unattended sessions, disable signing with `git config commit.gpgsign false --local` before dispatching agents. Re-enable after or note the caveat in the PR.

Multi-lens adversarial verification before executing security-critical crypto plans catches issues that single plan-checker misses — the parity-rigor lens found the vacuous-pass hole (TS KAT iterating empty arrays without length assertion) in both aad_vectors and seal_vectors.

Ultracode security review via a third-implementation verification (independently deriving the KAT ciphertext with OpenSSL) provides a true cross-implementation correctness proof, not just a code audit.
For sequential single-plan-per-wave phases that need node_modules and cargo cache, disabling worktrees is faster and more reliable than isolated worktrees requiring `pnpm i` per agent.

git filter-branch --msg-filter is the available mechanism for bulk commit reword in this environment (interactive rebase is not available). Use: `git filter-branch --msg-filter 'sed -E "1 s/^([a-z]+) [0-9][0-9A-Za-z.-]*: /\1: /"' <base>..HEAD`

When a Greptile review posts a thread alongside CodeRabbit, triage it with the same operating rule. Greptile caught a real asymmetry (TS >= 1 vs Rust == 1 for seal_vectors) that CodeRabbit missed in its initial pass.
The plan-phase adversarial verification workflow should run multiple rounds until zero remaining blockers — converging in 2 rounds is normal for a well-researched crypto phase.

friction: GSD main-tree install was a broken fragment with no gsd-tools.cjs, no update.md, and no file manifest — the normal /gsd-update flow couldn't run at all, requiring manual diagnosis to discover and force a clean reinstall.

CodeRabbit CLI --base main used local stale main, inflating the diff from 44 to 661 files and triggering the file-limit guard. Required diagnosing the divergence and rerunning with --base origin/main.
CodeRabbit showed 'Review skipped' on the initial PR check, creating false confidence that no PR-level threads would appear. The full review landed later after CI re-ran on the new head.
GSD commit helper consistently false-negatives (reports commit_failed while commits land) — required manual `git log` verification after every commit call.
1Password SSH signing blocks AFK subagent sessions, requiring commit signing to be disabled locally before dispatching background agents.
Root typecheck chain (`tsc -p tsconfig.scripts.json`) fails with @types/node resolution error — pre-existing but produces noisy false-failure in the full typecheck regression check.
The pattern-mapper PATTERNS.md is not auto-committed by the plan-phase workflow — requires an explicit commit step by the orchestrator or the file is lost.
git push is blocked in the sandbox environment — requires the dangerouslyDisableSandbox flag or a manual push step for every push operation.
